findings.description: The database password is interpolated into EC2 user data and written to a local PHP configuration file. User data is retrievable by processes with instance-level access and can be exposed through Terraform state or launch metadata, increasing the risk of credential disclosure.

The RDS instance has publicly_accessible = true, assigning it a public network endpoint. Although the shown security group restricts MySQL ingress to the VPC CIDR, this unnecessarily exposes the database to Internet routing and increases attack surface if security-group rules change or are bypassed.

storage_encrypted = false leaves RDS storage, backups, and snapshots unencrypted at rest, so an unauthorized party obtaining access to the underlying stored data can read it without a KMS decryption control.

The EC2 instance role grants s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* against every resource. Compromise of the application instance or its role credentials would permit broad control and data access across these AWS services.
